recommended_phases.title: Phase 1: Shared types + LeavePolicy module
recommended_phases.rationale: Foundation layer. LeaveType and LeaveStatus enums in shared-types have zero dependencies. LeavePolicy module depends only on shared-types. This establishes the policy lookup that balance and leave-request both need.

app_notes: Layer boundaries: presentation (routes + controllers), application (services), domain (entities + repository interfaces), infrastructure (repository implementations + DB). Dependencies flow inward: routes → controllers → services → repositories → DB. All modules expose only their index.ts. LeaveRequestService orchestrates across BalanceService and LeavePolicyService — it never touches their repositories directly. Every state-changing operation (submit, approve, reject, cancel) must write an audit record per GP-002. RBAC is enforced at the route level via middleware (employee vs manager vs hr_admin roles), never inline in services.
auth_contract: request.user: { id: string; role: UserRole } where UserRole = 'employee' | 'manager' | 'hr_admin'. JWT bearer token verified by an auth middleware that populates request.user. RBAC enforced by a requireRole(...) route-level guard. Employees can submit/cancel their own requests and view their own balances. Managers can approve/reject requests for their direct reports and view team leave requests. HR admins can configure policies and view all balances/requests.
error_response_contract: Standard error shape: { error: string; code: string }. Validation failure → HTTP 400 (code: VALIDATION_ERROR). Authentication failure → 401 (code: UNAUTHORIZED). Authorization failure → 403 (code: FORBIDDEN). Not found → 404 (code: NOT_FOUND). Insufficient balance → 422 (code: INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE). Overlapping leave request → 409 (code: OVERLAPPING_REQUEST).
